title: A large world in Rust: streamed cells around an anchor, pure cell builders, the ground drawn near the camera
note: Register game.streaming, build cells in pure game.cell_content builders, move the anchor every tick, and keep what entered or left in the world.
intent: A world bigger than one level streams in square cells, never as everything built at reset. Register game.streaming(Streaming::grid(64.0).sim_radius(1)) once and set an anchor with sim.stream.set_anchor("player", at) in on_reset and every tick. A game.cell_content builder makes a cell from its inputs alone (bounds, its own rng, inputs.model(path)) on a worker thread, reading no world and no clock: things for the sim, CellBuild::model and CellBuild::group (inputs.scatter for forests) for what draws, and those draw on their own while the cell is in view. In on_update take sim.stream.entered() things into the world and drop the cells sim.stream.left() names. TerrainTiles::procedural(65, height) gives the sim its ground (sim.stream.ground) and, with game.stream_colliders, a collider per tile; the ground on screen is the game's own terrain patch around the camera from the same height function. Per cell at most 256 things, 64 colliders, 4096 instances; past one it enters empty, named stream-invalid. A cell model's impostor bakes only if wire calls game.impostor_bake(|gfx| ..). Save with sim.stream.snapshot() beside the world; capture with frame.cells_debug() from above.
port: The world's owner registers game.streaming and the anchor; each facet may register its own cell_content builder and keeps only the things of its type.

evidence.note: Streaming::grid, anchors, pure cell builders with things, models and groups, entered and left, terrain tiles and their colliders, the caps, snapshot and restore, cells_debug.
Terrain::from_fn and frame.terrain draw the ground the camera sees.
